cues.en: Today on Applied Science I'm going to talk about these e ink or e paper displays.
cues.zh: 今天在 Applied Science 上，我要聊聊这些电子墨水或电子纸显示屏。

cues.en: These things were made popular in the Kindle and other e readers
cues.zh: 这些东西因为 Kindle 和其他电子阅读器而流行起来

cues.en: and now they're available on the hobbyist market and you can play with putting them in all kinds of different projects.
cues.zh: 现在它们已经能在爱好者市场上买到，你可以试着把它们放进各种不同的项目里。

cues.en: Of course one of their signature features is that they retain the image even when it's not connected to anything at all. So it takes literally zero power
cues.zh: 当然，它们的标志性特点之一是：即使完全不连接任何东西，也能保留图像。所以字面意义上零功耗

cues.en: to maintain the image.
cues.zh: 就能维持图像。

cues.en: And of course the
cues.zh: 当然，它的

cues.en: look of it is much more like paper than it is a liquid crystal display.
cues.zh: 外观比液晶显示屏更像纸。

cues.en: They also have these interesting red, white, and black displays which are pretty cool.
cues.zh: 它们还有这种很有意思的红白黑显示屏，挺酷的。

cues.en: It's not a color filter. We'll talk about the tech that goes into these but it's actually really unusual how these work.
cues.zh: 它不是彩色滤光片。我们会聊聊里面用的技术，但它们的工作原理其实非常不寻常。

cues.en: So the setup I have here today is a Teensy microcontroller
cues.zh: 所以我今天这里的配置是一个 Teensy 微控制器

cues.en: that we're programming through the Arduino interface
cues.zh: 我们通过 Arduino 接口给它编程

cues.en: and it's driving this display over the Spy Bus. You can see I bought this one from Waveshare.
cues.zh: 并通过 SPI 总线驱动这块显示屏。你看，这块是我从 Waveshare 买的。

cues.en: And then we have this glorious scope from Tektronix on loan from Tektronix to monitor the spy bus.
cues.zh: 然后还有这台很棒的 Tektronix 示波器，是 Tektronix 借给我们的，用来监测 SPI 总线。

cues.en: Waveshare is not a manufacturer of these panels but they are a,
cues.zh: Waveshare 不是这些面板的制造商，但它是……

cues.en: I guess a distributor that also makes these breakout boards. So it's very convenient to have a board that converts the flat flex that's on the display to this
cues.zh: 我猜算是分销商，同时也做这些转接板。所以有块板子把显示屏上的柔性排线转成这个

cues.en: pin header.
cues.zh: 排针，非常方便。

cues.en: And also they provided some firmware which is a great starting point. So let's zoom in on the display and check out some demos.
cues.zh: 另外他们还提供了一些固件，是个很好的起点。那我们把镜头拉近到显示屏，看看几个演示。

cues.en: Okay. I'm going to run the demo that comes direct from Waveshare.
cues.zh: 好，我来跑一下Waveshare自带的那个演示。

cues.en: It's just two frames and so it's compiling and downloading.
cues.zh: 就两帧，正在编译和下载。

cues.en: And you'll see when the image transitions,
cues.zh: 你会看到图像切换的时候，

cues.en: first you see the inverse of it, then all white, then all black, then the image. This is the frame.
cues.zh: 先看到反色，然后全白，再全黑，最后才出图像。这就是那一帧。

cues.en: And then it's gonna switch back to the first frame. And as you can see it's a pretty long process.
cues.zh: 然后它会切回第一帧。可以看到这个过程挺长的。

cues.en: So you can't change
cues.zh: 所以你不走完那套好几秒的

cues.en: any part of the display without going through that entire multi second
cues.zh: 刷新流程，

cues.en: refresh routine.
cues.zh: 就没法改动显示内容的任何部分。

cues.en: And the early Kindle and other e reader type things had this same
cues.zh: 早期的Kindle和其他电子阅读器也有同样的

cues.en: characteristic to them. You can't just update the screen. You have to clear it entirely.
cues.zh: 特性。你不能只更新屏幕，必须整个清掉重来。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 不过，

cues.en: if you know how tweak the firmware, you can make the screen do anything you want. Actually, interestingly, the controller is very programmable
cues.zh: 如果你知道怎么改固件，就能让屏幕做任何你想做的事。其实有意思的是，这个控制器可编程性很强

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: it's sort of security by obscurity. You you can load any values you want into the registers and cause it to do anything.
cues.zh: 这算是靠隐蔽性来保证安全。你可以往寄存器里写任意值，让它做任何事。

cues.en: You may hurt the display, but let's let's take a look and see what's going on.
cues.zh: 可能会弄坏屏幕，不过咱们来看看究竟是怎么回事。

cues.en: Okay. So I'm gonna load up the demo reel that I made with my custom firmware,
cues.zh: 好，我现在加载用我自定义固件做的演示片段，

cues.en: and we'll see how fast the update is. So the first one clears it. That's just a standard update.
cues.zh: 看看更新有多快。第一个是清屏，那就是一次标准更新。

cues.en: And now you can see the frame rate is about three hertz. So we don't have to flash the whole display
cues.zh: 现在可以看到帧率大约是3赫兹。这样我们就不必刷新整个屏幕

cues.en: and we can update any part of it
cues.zh: 而且可以在三分之一秒内

cues.en: within a third of a second.
cues.zh: 更新它的任意部分。

cues.en: This one shows what an animation would look like at at close to three hertz.
cues.zh: 这个展示了接近三赫兹的动画会是什么样子。

cues.en: And you can see that I'm drawing text up here and I'm slowly moving the text in the x direction across the screen to prevent burn in which we'll we'll talk about a little bit later. The ball going around in circle doesn't really cause much burn in. But you will see if you look closely
cues.zh: 可以看到我在这里绘制文字，并慢慢将文字沿x方向在屏幕上移动，以防止烧屏，我们稍后会讨论这个。球绕圈运动其实不会造成太多烧屏。但仔细看你会发现

cues.en: there's a ghost image as it was going to a full white screen. So you can still see that ghost image. So now we'll go back to Waveshare.
cues.zh: 当它要变成全白屏幕时，会留下残影。所以你仍然能看到那个残影。现在我们回到Waveshare。

cues.en: These are all full updates as you can see because it's going through the cycling.
cues.zh: 这些都是全屏刷新，如你所见，因为它正在走刷新循环。

cues.en: That should look familiar.
cues.zh: 这应该看起来很熟悉。

cues.en: You can see when it's done cycling, there's no more ghost left. Like, text is completely clean.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，当刷新循环结束后，残影就没有了。文字完全干净。

cues.en: When it's going through its image update process,
cues.zh: 当它进行图像更新过程时，

cues.en: you can see a little bit of remnant. So
cues.zh: 你能看到一点残留。所以

cues.en: we'll talk about this a little bit more but I think that the pulse sequence I've come up with is more or less safe. But it's possible that if you,
cues.zh: 我们稍后会再详细讨论这个，但我认为我提出的脉冲序列基本上算是安全的。但有可能如果你，

cues.en: you know, somewhat abuse the display like this
cues.zh: 你知道，这样有点滥用显示屏

cues.en: eventually there will be burn in, permanent maybe.
cues.zh: 最终会出现烧屏，可能是永久性的。

cues.en: Certainly short term burn in for sure.
cues.zh: 短期烧屏肯定是有的。

cues.en: Let's talk about how these things actually work and then it'll make it clear why we have this problem with burn in. So if we were to cut one of these displays and look at the cross section from the side we would have sort of a smooth top
cues.zh: 我们来谈谈这些东西实际是如何工作的，然后就能清楚为什么会有烧屏问题。如果我们切开其中一个显示屏，从侧面看横截面，会有一个光滑的顶部

cues.en: which is an electrode and we'll call that common.
cues.zh: 那是一个电极，我们称之为公共电极。

cues.en: And then within the display there's a whole bunch of chambers.
cues.zh: 然后显示器内部有一大堆腔室。

cues.en: And these are not necessarily pixels they're just
cues.zh: 这些不一定是像素，它们只是

cues.en: little chambers within the display.
cues.zh: 显示器内的小腔室。

cues.en: And within each of those there are positive and negative
cues.zh: 每个腔室里都有带正电和带负电的

cues.en: particles.
cues.zh: 粒子。

cues.en: And they're submersed or they're suspended in a fluid, oil of some kind.
cues.zh: 它们浸没或悬浮在某种流体中，比如某种油。

cues.en: And the trick is that
cues.zh: 关键在于

cues.en: the positively charged particles are black let's say and the negatively charged particles are white. So if we put an electrode
cues.zh: 带正电的粒子是黑色的，带负电的粒子是白色的。所以如果我们把一个电极

cues.en: array on the bottom and in this case each one of these is a pixel
cues.zh: 阵列放在底部，这里每一个都是一个像素

cues.en: and if we put a positive
cues.zh: 然后如果我们在这里加正

cues.en: voltage up here and a negative voltage here the field will cause the negative particle to migrate to the top and the positive particle to migrate to the bottom. So what we'll end up with is white particles if those are negative going to the top
cues.zh: 电压，那里加负电压，电场会使负粒子迁移到顶部，正粒子迁移到底部。最终我们会得到白色粒子，如果这些是负粒子的话，它们会去到像素的顶部

cues.en: of this pixel and then as we scan across we can change the fields for each one of these pixels.
cues.zh: 然后当我们扫描时，我们可以改变每个像素的电场。

cues.en: Pretty cool.
cues.zh: 挺酷的。

cues.en: In its most basic form you could just put one voltage across this thing and if you're scanning through all the pixels you could say okay, you know, positive on top, negative on bottom for this one, positive on top, negative and scan through it. And the display would work at least once or twice.
cues.zh: 在最基本的形式中，你可以只在这个东西上加一个电压，如果你扫描所有像素，你可以说，好，正极在上，负极在下，正极在上，负极，然后扫描过去。显示器至少能工作一两次。

cues.en: But the problem is with electrostatics
cues.zh: 但问题在于静电

cues.en: and fields like this eventually the parts of the display will become charged themselves. And so if you keep putting this electric field
cues.zh: 和这样的电场，最终显示器的部件本身会带电。所以如果你一直在这个显示器上施加

cues.en: on the display
cues.zh: 电场

cues.en: eventually
cues.zh: 最终

cues.en: this positive charge will accumulate in the display and then your display won't work anymore because when you put a voltage on there you're gonna be fighting against all the charge that's in there.
cues.zh: 这些正电荷会在显示器中积累，然后你的显示器就不能工作了，因为当你施加电压时，你将与那里所有的电荷对抗。

cues.en: So one of the tricks to driving these things is you actually put an AC voltage on this and
cues.zh: 所以，驱动这类设备的一个诀窍是，实际上要给它加上交流电压，然后

cues.en: rapidly cycle it to prevent it from becoming polarized.
cues.zh: 快速地切换电压，防止它发生极化。

cues.en: There's actually a similar problem with LCDs.
cues.zh: LCD 其实也有类似的问题。

cues.en: You can't run an LCD with just DC voltage because it will polarize
cues.zh: LCD 不能只用直流电压驱动，因为它会发生极化

cues.en: and stop working.
cues.zh: 然后停止工作。

cues.en: If you search around on
cues.zh: 如果你在

cues.en: e paper distributor sites you'll see that some of the newer displays are actually rated for what they call partial refresh. So basically doing this without any flashing or flickering. Get a new image on the screen without any of that.
cues.zh: 电子纸经销商网站上搜索，就会发现一些较新的显示屏实际上支持一种叫作局部刷新的功能。基本上就是在不闪烁的情况下完成刷新，让屏幕显示新图像，而完全没有这些现象。

cues.en: And I think the trick is they've basically just loosened the
cues.zh: 我觉得诀窍在于，他们基本上只是放宽了

cues.en: of the usage restrictions and so they're saying okay you can bend the rules a little bit by putting just a DC voltage on there to get a quick update but then you better do a full refresh at some point near in the future. And I think
cues.zh: 使用限制的要求，所以他们的意思是：可以稍微变通一下，给它加上直流电压来快速更新，但之后最好在不久的将来某个时候进行一次完整刷新。而且我觉得

cues.en: you know the
cues.zh: 你知道，

cues.en: reason that it's
cues.zh: 之所以

cues.en: hard to find instructions on how to do this is because they know that you're gonna degrade the panels performance if you don't have the right routine.
cues.zh: 很难找到具体怎么做的说明，是因为他们知道，如果没有正确的操作流程，显示面板的性能会逐渐下降。

cues.en: So it takes a little bit of experimentation to get all this working.
cues.zh: 所以，要让这一切正常工作，需要进行一些尝试。

cues.en: Additionally this display that I'm using this 4.2 inches actually has
cues.zh: 另外，我正在使用的这块 4.2 英寸显示屏，实际上有

cues.en: two complete frame buffers inside of it and so it knows it keeps one frame buffer as like the currently displayed
cues.zh: 两个完整的帧缓冲区，它会把其中一个帧缓冲区作为当前显示的

cues.en: image and then the other frame buffer is the image that it wants to display next.
cues.zh: 图像，另一个帧缓冲区则存放它接下来想要显示的图像。

cues.en: And what it does it knows that if there's
cues.zh: 它知道，如果出现这种情况，

cues.en: if this pixel or if this pixel is currently white then it knows that all the positive charges in the top or whatever
cues.zh: 如果这个像素或这个像素当前是白色的，那么它就知道顶部所有的正电荷，或者类似这样的电荷

cues.en: and if it knows that it wants to convert that pixel to black in the next frame it actually gives it a different sequence of positive and negative voltages than if it's going to stay white in the next frame.
cues.zh: 如果它知道下一帧要把这个像素变成黑色，它实际施加的正负电压序列，就会和下一帧保持白色时的不同。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: the display has this thing internally called the lookup table
cues.zh: 显示屏内部有个东西叫查找表

cues.en: and it basically has a set of waveforms that we're going to put on these pixels
cues.zh: 里面基本上存着一组要施加到这些像素上的波形

cues.en: and the waveform is selected based on what the pixel was in the last frame and what the pixel is in the new frame.
cues.zh: 具体选择哪种波形，取决于像素上一帧的颜色，以及新一帧要显示的颜色。

cues.en: And it seems kind of overkill but they obviously they wouldn't go through all this trouble if it wasn't necessary.
cues.zh: 这听起来有点小题大做，但如果不是必要的，他们显然不会费这么大工夫。

cues.en: So coming up with this correct drive sequence is basically the secret to all these all of these e paper displays.
cues.zh: 所以，得出正确的驱动序列，基本上就是所有这些电子纸显示屏的秘诀。

cues.en: So what about these red ones? You might think well it's probably just a color filter. I mean it's probably just white pixels underneath the red thing but that's actually not what's going on. It's a true three color pixel. It can select whether it's going to be red, black, or white. And I searched around and it took a long time to find this out but I think the way it works is kind of like this.
cues.zh: 那这些红色的像素呢？你可能会想，它大概只是一个颜色滤镜。也就是说，红色东西下面可能只是白色像素，但实际情况并不是这样。这是真正的三色像素，可以选择显示红色、黑色或白色。我查了很久才弄清楚，不过我觉得它的工作方式大概是这样的。

cues.en: Imagine that you have
cues.zh: 想象一下，你有一些

cues.en: black pixels
cues.zh: 黑色像素

cues.en: that are small and positively charged
cues.zh: 它们体积很小，并且带正电

cues.en: And then you have really large red ones
cues.zh: 然后还有一些体积很大的红色像素

cues.en: that are also positively charged.
cues.zh: 它们也带正电。

cues.en: And then you've got small white ones that are negatively charged.
cues.zh: 然后你还有带负电的白色小颗粒。

cues.en: So then if you put this thing between the two electrodes
cues.zh: 那么如果你把这个东西放在两个电极之间

cues.en: the large ones and the small black ones will have the same
cues.zh: 大的颗粒和小的黑色颗粒会受到相同的

cues.en: motive force applied to them. If we put this
cues.zh: 驱动力。如果我们把

cues.en: field here minus
cues.zh: 这里的电场设为

cues.en: on the bottom and positive on the top both the red and the black will be attracted to the top let's say. But the red ones are going to move more slowly because they are bigger even though the charge is about the same and it's in this viscous sort of fluid.
cues.zh: 底部为负、顶部为正，那么红色和黑色颗粒都会被吸引到顶部，比如说。但红色颗粒会移动得更慢，因为它们更大，尽管电荷量差不多，而且它们处于这种黏性流体中。

cues.en: So if you put a voltage on here quickly
cues.zh: 所以如果你在这里快速施加电压

cues.en: the black ones will make it to the top faster than the red ones and the pixel will turn black.
cues.zh: 黑色颗粒会比红色颗粒更快到达顶部，像素就会变黑。

cues.en: If you want to turn the pixel red what you do is you first make it black so that you're in this configuration with the white ones in the bottom, the red ones kind of in the middle, and the black ones at the top. Then you switch the field causing the black ones to move down and the white ones to move up. But before they have a chance to switch places the red ones will actually end up being the ones that are closest to the top and the black ones will be kind of below and the white ones haven't started moving just yet.
cues.zh: 如果你想让像素变红，你要先让它变黑，这样就处于这种配置：白色颗粒在底部，红色颗粒在中间，黑色颗粒在顶部。然后你切换电场，让黑色颗粒向下移动，白色颗粒向上移动。但在它们有机会交换位置之前，红色颗粒实际上会成为最靠近顶部的颗粒，黑色颗粒会在下面，而白色颗粒还没开始移动。

cues.en: I think each manufacturer has their own special trick of how this works.
cues.zh: 我觉得每个制造商都有自己特殊的实现诀窍。

cues.en: And even searching patents and things it's actually very difficult to figure out what's going on here.
cues.zh: 甚至搜索专利之类的东西，实际上也很难弄清楚这里到底是怎么回事。

cues.en: But when we start looking at the code you'll see there's special pulse sequences to get the red ones to the top. It's amazingly effective. I mean it's a very high contrast
cues.zh: 但当我们开始看代码时，你会发现有一些特殊的脉冲序列能把红色粒子推到顶部。效果惊人地好。我的意思是，对比度非常高

cues.en: sort of display and there's no, I mean you can see the background is actually a little bit white compared to a
cues.zh: 的显示效果，而且没有，我是说你能看到背景实际上比

cues.en: black and white only e paper. You can see the background on this one is much paler. It's much truer to white. This one's a little bit reddish probably because those red particles aren't fully at the bottom.
cues.zh: 纯黑白电子纸要稍微白一点。你能看到这个的背景要淡得多，更接近真正的白色。这个有点偏红，可能是因为那些红色粒子没有完全沉到底部。
